editorNote: Two AI-adjacent policy moves bookend today's edition — Denmark's verbal-defense mandate for take-home assignments and Amazon's outsized gas-plant footprint for AI infrastructure — alongside a new Claude Code feature for coordinating agent sessions, a privacy-driven Fastmail launch, an efficiency benchmark that muddies the Apple-Silicon narrative, and an essay defending programming as hard work in its own right.

stories.headline: Amazon's Texas AI data center plans a gas plant bigger than the country's biggest coal plant
stories.summary: Amazon is building a 7.65-gigawatt gas power plant for a data center project in Pecos County, Texas, with state permits allowing up to 33 million tons of CO2 emissions a year — more than the country's largest coal plant. Land clearing has begun and the site would run off-grid initially.
stories.whyItMatters: It puts real numbers behind the AI buildout's energy cost, and sits awkwardly next to Amazon's pledge to hit net-zero emissions by 2040.

sourceLinks.title: Amazon Is Creating the Biggest Pollution Source in the Country

stories.headline: Denmark orders high schoolers to verbally defend take-home assignments to combat AI cheating
stories.summary: Denmark's Ministry of Education now requires upper-secondary students to verbally defend any written assignment done at home, alongside screen monitoring and content firewalls during exams — effective immediately for roughly 9,000 students in its two-year exam-prep program.
stories.whyItMatters: It's one of the more concrete government responses yet to AI-assisted cheating, trading take-home trust for in-person verification rather than banning tools outright.

sourceLinks.title: Danish high schoolers will have to verbally defend written assignments, in government move to combat AI cheating

stories.headline: Claude Code lets your coding sessions message each other
stories.summary: Anthropic shipped cross-session messaging in Claude Code: one session can find and message another on the same machine, or reply across machines via Remote Control, using new ListAgents and SendMessage tools. A message is plain text only, never full conversation history or files, and the feature requires Claude Code v2.1.224+ on macOS or Linux.
stories.whyItMatters: It formalizes a pattern developers were already working around — sessions in separate worktrees coordinating on the same codebase — without exposing files or a full transcript between them.

sourceLinks.title: Message your other Claude Code sessions

stories.headline: Fastmail launches an EU data region, storing email on its own Amsterdam servers
stories.summary: Fastmail now lets any customer choose to store primary email data in an EU region built on its own Amsterdam infrastructure rather than its existing US locations, at no extra cost. Users with European billing addresses were pre-migrated; everyone else can switch anytime in account settings.
stories.whyItMatters: It's a compliance and trust play for users who don't want data leaving the EU, built on owned infrastructure rather than a rented cloud region.

stories.headline: A Dell XPS 13 with Intel's Core 5 320 beats most Apple Silicon Macs on power efficiency
stories.summary: In Jeff Geerling's Linpack benchmark tests, a Dell XPS 13 running Intel's Core 5 320 chip hit 6.21 Gflops per watt, beating the MacBook Neo's 5.38 and every Mac Studio tested — losing only to the M4 Mac Mini's 7.57.
stories.whyItMatters: It complicates the assumption that ARM chips automatically win on performance-per-watt, suggesting Apple's efficiency lead owes as much to design choices as to architecture.

sourceLinks.title: Want energy efficiency? Dude, you're getting a Dell

stories.headline: A programmer pushes back on 'code was never the hard part'
stories.summary: Responding to a common tech-circle refrain that coding is easy and the real skill is deciding what to build, developer Ivan Rašić argues the framing insults programmers: high salaries, brutal interview bars, and decades of legends in the field all say coding is genuinely hard — and the answer to code-vs-domain-knowledge is both, not either.
stories.whyItMatters: It's a rebuttal to the current wave of AI-coding-agent triumphalism that treats implementation as a solved, low-value commodity.

sourceLinks.title: "Code was never the hard part" is an insult to all programmers
